source.title: On the Neural Tangent Kernel of Deep Networks with Orthogonal Initialization
source.authors: Wei Huang; Wei-Tao Du; R. Xu

record.tranche_reason: Compares orthogonal and Gaussian initialization and reports training dynamics across learning rates, widths, and depths; this is a conceptual test of initialization and training speed.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports NTK and weight-change results, but those do not directly measure the training-error outcomes named by the claim versions. Figure 3 uses τ to measure time to a threshold accuracy; its plotted values are not described numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares training speed under orthogonal and variance-matched Gaussian initialization, testing V4 empirically and through an argument about convergence rates in the NTK regime. It does not test V1: its training experiments use fully connected networks and do not establish the claimed convolutional-network training-error endpoints.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that orthogonal initialization provides no training-speed advantage in the NTK regime, while it can accelerate training and improve generalization outside that regime at large learning rates or depths when initialization variances put the nonlinear activation near its linear regime.
record.recipe_differences: Uses CIFAR-10 with tanh fully connected networks and compares orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; reports training speed and accuracy dynamics rather than final training classification error. It also includes small-learning-rate comparisons on CIFAR-10 and MNIST.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative training-speed difference changes with learning rate and depth; the paper reports larger differences at larger learning rates and greater depth. Its threshold-accuracy τ analysis also varies width and depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Orthogonal initialization also improves test accuracy and generalization in the reported deep-network experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal initialization can improve generalization relative to Gaussian initialization in deep tanh fully connected networks under the tested settings.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The large-learning-rate/depth results are primarily presented as curves; the text gives no numeric training-error endpoints. The CIFAR-10 comparisons use D = 256 samples, tanh fully connected networks and average results over 30 instantiations; they do not test corrupted or random labels.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Figure 3’s separate width/depth curves are retained as one aggregate figure-only row because the plotted values are not specified in the text.

untested.parts: The convolutional-network claim, near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut controls, and the stated alternative training recipes.
A systematic activation-matching comparison, maximum trainable depth, and empirical training of 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks with orthogonal kernels.
Loss recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence thresholds.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate comparisons, and Fixup training without normalization.

missing.what: Matched training dynamics with no appreciable orthogonal speed advantage: CIFAR-10 tanh networks at L=5, n=800, SGD learning rate 0.001; MNIST ReLU networks at L=9, n=1600, reported RMSProp learning rate 0.00001. Record training loss and accuracy comparisons separately.

Nearly identical training loss and accuracy under full-batch gradient descent for tanh fully connected networks at L=3, n=400 and L=7, n=800, using 256 CIFAR-10 samples, learning rate 0.0001, and 10,000 steps.

The study's theoretical argument that matched orthogonal and Gaussian initializations have identical limiting NTKs and equal convergence rates in the infinite-width lazy-training regime, including FCNs and CNNs.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Absence of near-zero training-error endpoints does not justify a V1 limits_scope verdict. The supplied text does not permit numerical curve extraction. Section 5 and the Figure 2 caption give inconsistent dataset-size descriptions, so the record's blanket assertion of 256 samples across all comparisons should not be treated as established.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label or corrupted-label training; convolutional networks; CIFAR-100; Adam; smaller models and early stopping; whether training classification error reaches zero or near zero.
Activation-matched initializations beyond the reported tanh experiments; very deep plain tanh networks trained with orthogonal weights at 10,000 layers; orthogonal convolution kernels.
